chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Shayban narrated to us in Sha'ban in the year three and seventy of the two hundred, saying: Ali ibn Sayf ibn 'Umayra narrated to us, from his father, from Humran ibn A'yun, that he said:

I described to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) a man who believes in the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and exempts himself from his enemy, and believes in all that he says, except that he says: 'They have disagreed among themselves, and they are the leading Imams, and I do not know which of them is the Imam. And if they agree upon one man, we will submit to his word, and I have known that the matter is among them - may Allah have mercy on them all.'
He (Abu Abdillah) said: 'If this man dies, he dies a death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah).'

And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy - devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring to one another decorative speech in delusion. And if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and that which they invent.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on doubting the identity of the Imams according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the 'waiting for consensus' (intizar) approach, declaring it a 'death of ignorance' because it implies uncertainty in the divinely appointed Imamate rather than firm belief in the specific Twelve. This narration underscores the Shia doctrine of explicit designation (nass), where doubt in the identity of the Imam equates to a return to pre-Islamic ignorance. The concluding verse highlights how this doubt is fueled by the 'deceptive speech' of Shayatin, mirroring the confusion between truth and falsehood.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (19) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Yahya bin Zakariyya bin Shayban from Ali bin Sayf bin Omayra from his father that Hamran bin A’yun had said:

I have told Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) about a man, who believes in Amirul Mo’mineen (as) as the guardian, exempts himself from his (Ali’s) opponents and believes in all that Amirul Mo’mineen (as) has said but he says: They have disagreed among themselves whereas they are the leading imams and I do not know which of them is the imam. If they have agreed upon one man, we will submit to his orders. I have believed that the imamate is among them. May Allah have mercy upon them all.
Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) said: “He will die as an unbeliever.”

The same was narrated by Ali bin Sayf from his brother al-Husayn from Mu’ath bin Muslim from Imam as-Sadiq (as). Let those of understanding, who believe in the guardianship of the infallible imams of Ahlul Bayt, ponder on the traditions narrated from the Prophet (S), Imam Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) and Imam Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) talking about those, who have doubted anyone of the twelve imams or have spent a night without knowing their imam. These traditions have considered such people as unbelievers, hypocrites and polytheists. Let them also ponder on the traditions that have said: “Whoever denies one of the alive imams is as if he has denied the dead ones.” Let men of understanding look well for the one, whom they will follow, without being deceived by fancies and falsehood in order no to deviate from the path of the truth. Let them know well who will be the means between them and their Creator, Who is One and Only, whereas the devils are so many. Allah has said: “…The Shaitans from among men and jinn, some of them suggesting to others varnished falsehood to deceive (them).” We pray Allah to save us and our brothers in faith from deviating from the truth and guidance and not to let us welter in the abysses of confusion and perishment. We look forward to His mercy; He is merciful to the believers.
